subject: both Event List header schemas on an English Logic, read through the product's own header path
question: What does the Event pane's header actually render in en-US at each level, and on which role and attribute?

host.note: The note-level reading required a region to be selected; the selection was made by writing AXSelected from an empty selection and reading it back. Logic's own preference reads `AppleLanguages = (en)`; `en-US` is this repository's key for that label set.

reverify.expected: REVERIFY PASS — region-level schema, titles unchanged  (or: note-level schema, titles unchanged)
reverify.cost: live; Logic running with the Event pane open; read-only; seconds. Either pane state is accepted, because which one is showing depends on the selection rather than on the check.

method: The probe walks the path `readHeaders` walks: the Event pane's table, its `AXHeader`, and that header's children, reading each child's role, subrole and `AXTitle`, and tagging each row with the surface and path it was read from. Reading the same elements the product reads is what lets a coverage claim name the role and attribute the product actually uses rather than a role that merely happened to carry the same string somewhere else in the window. Both schemas were captured: the region list with no region selected, and a region's events after one region was selected.

observations.selection: one MIDI region selected, help reading `Region starts at 1 bar and ends at 2 bars`

observations.note: unsupported. A reader looking for titles there finds nothing and cannot tell that from an empty table; the titles live on each column's header cell.

observations.what: how the note level was reached
observations.action: AXSelected written true on one region from an empty selection, then read back
observations.note: a write to AXSelected TOGGLES rather than sets, so it lands on exactly one region only from a selection that was read as empty first

conclusion: On an English Logic the Event List renders two header schemas, both as `AXSortButton` buttons read by `AXTitle`: `L, M, Position, Name, Trk, Length` for the region list and `L, M, Position, Status, Ch, Num, Val, Length/Info` for a selected region's events. All eleven distinct strings match the canonicals `AXLocalePolicy` already carried, which were English by convention and had never been observed — including the three abbreviations `Ch`, `Num` and `Val`, where an expansion to `Channel`, `Number` or `Value` would have failed to match on an English Logic exactly as the `Event` tab literal once did. The read path is the header cell, not `AXColumnTitles`, which the table does not support.
limits: Titles, not identity. That a column titled `Position` carries positions is a separate claim; this records what the header renders.
One project on one host. Column titles are a property of the application, but a Logic update can relabel them, which is what the reverify exists to catch.
Nothing here measures the ko-KR or ja-JP forms. The Korean variants already in the label file remain without provenance and are unaffected by this record.
The note-level reading is of ONE selected region with one event row. A schema is not row-dependent, but nothing here establishes that a region with other event types renders the same eight columns.
